text:
lee: heads up — support just escalated a p99 latency regression for a hosted customer (AcmeCorp) on /v1/generate. Reported after the 23:00 deploy. p95 unchanged-ish but p99 jumped a lot.
lee: sample from the customer: request_id=acme-req-9f3a model=text-llama-7b seq_len=1024 tokens_out=256 region=eu-west-1 p95=210ms p99=900ms (their baseline p99 ~260ms). they sent 5 traces and one attached a full curl.
sam: can you paste the curl and one full runtime trace? also which pool - shared/hosted?
lee: pasted below (redacted keys). pool=hosted-eu, path=/v1/generate, reproducible with their prompt.
lee: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-llama-7b","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":256}'
```
sam: thanks. first guess — we flipped the kernel-selector tweak in the last runtime build that biases toward SDPA kernels for >512 seq to reduce perf for long context. If SDPA path on that GPU/driver combo regresses, p99 can burst. jess any recent changes in FlashAttention/SDPA compile flags?
jess: yep — we landed two changes last week: 1) default to SDPA for seq>512 in kernel_picker, and 2) bump nvrtc/clang flags to enable newer math intrinsics. Both could interact badly with the vendor kernel. we also updated the FlashAttention shim to prefer fp16 kernels.
toni: infra side — we updated the ROCM runtime on eu-west cluster (driver 5.3.x -> 5.4.x) at the same time as the runtime deploy for that region. That may change perf behavior of vendor kernels.
max: so three moving parts: kernel_picker, compile flags, driver. we need repro on staging or quick mitigation.
sam: repro plan: reproduce a batch of requests matching their seq length and single-request pattern (no batching). run with 1) current build, 2) force `REDWOOD_KERSEL=legacy` (old picker), 3) disable SDPA, 4) force FlashAttention. collect p95/p99 and kernel names. Toni can we spin a eu-west staging node with the same driver?
toni: I can spin up a node with the upgraded driver and one pinned to old driver. gave a name: staging-eu-kerneltest. ETA 25m.
lee: customer provided a short prompt that reproduces locally. they attached traces showing kernel names: `sdpa_kern_v12`, `sdpa_kern_v12`, `kv_merge`. older traces had `flashattn_fwd_fp16_v7`.
jess: interesting — that indicates kernel selector picked SDPA kernels. please run the runtime with `--kernel-toggle=prefer-flash` to force FlashAttention and see. also we have env flags: `REDWOOD_ENABLE_FLASHATTN=1` / `REDWOOD_ENABLE_SDPA=0`.
sam: quick mitigation options: 1) hotfix: change kernel_picker to bias flash for model=text-llama-7b on eu-west pool (prefer-flash), 2) rollback kernel-selector change for hosted-eu, 3) patch driver or revert compile flags. fastest is (1) or (2).
max: we should avoid full rollback unless required. patch weighted picker for that model/tier seems safe. we need telemetry though — add a canary that forces flash for 1% of traffic and measure p99.
lee: customer is asking for an ETA, reported this is impacting user-facing latency. they asked for a temporary config toggle. can we flip env var for their org?
sam: we have org-scoped runtime overrides. I can push `REDWOOD_ENABLE_SDPA=0` for AcmeCorp route via the routing config. I'll do a targeted override and monitor.
perf-bot: Auto-alert triggered: p99 spike on hosted-eu /v1/generate (model=text-llama-7b). Graphs: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/hosted-eu/p99
toni: staging nodes up. running the four experiments now.
(30m passes)
sam: quick results from staging:
- current build (kernel_picker=opt, driver=5.4): p95=220ms p99=890ms, top kernels sdpa_v12
- force-legacy-picker (kernel_picker=legacy): p95=215ms p99=270ms, kernels flashattn_fwd_fp16_v7
- disable SDPA (REDWOOD_ENABLE_SDPA=0): p95=218ms p99=280ms
- force FlashAttention (prefer-flash): p95=214ms p99=260ms
So SDPA path is the culprit on this hardware/driver combo.
jess: that matches my hunch. compile flags probably made the SDPA kernels faster generally but introduced tail-case instability. we should revert the kernel_picker bias change and roll a targeted fix for kernels.
max: plan of action:
- Immediate: sam to push org-scoped override for AcmeCorp (REDWOOD_ENABLE_SDPA=0) and create a 1% canary that prefers flash for hosted-eu. (owner: sam)
- Short (today): revert kernel_picker bias in hosted-eu and deploy. (owner: sam + eng-runtime)
- Medium (48h): jess to start a kernel bisect job to identify offending compile flag/SDPA variant, add unit perf test that measures tail latency for long seq on eu-west driver. (owner: jess)
- Infra: toni to pin eu-west driver down if rollout of driver caused issues, coordinate with cloud provider. (owner: toni)
- Support: lee to update AcmeCorp with ETA and temporary toggle. (owner: lee)
lee: I told AcmeCorp we have a mitigation and will apply a temporary toggle, gave ETA ~30-60m. they asked for a postmortem.
sam: I pushed the org override: `route.acmecorp.env.REDWOOD_ENABLE_SDPA=0` in hosted-eu. monitoring shows p99 dropping to ~260ms for their traffic within 2 minutes.
lee: customer confirms p99 improved in their region, thanked us. :thumbsup:
jess: next steps for durable fix: revert picker bias in main branch + add a regression test against p99 for seq=1024 on eu-west infra in CI. also add a config flag for kernel_picker tuning by model family.
max: please log an incident and follow the postmortem template (owner: sam). include the canary graphs and the bisect matrix.
sam: will file incident #2023-IR-72 and assign. I'll include repro steps and the commands to reproduce:
```bash
# reproduce locally against staging node
export REDWOOD_ENABLE_SDPA=1
export REDWOOD_ENABLE_FLASHATTN=1
# run bench client that mimics single-request long-context
python tools/bench_single.py --host staging-eu-kerneltest --model text-llama-7b --seq 1024 --n=500
# toggle SDPA off
export REDWOOD_ENABLE_SDPA=0
python tools/bench_single.py --host staging-eu-kerneltest --model text-llama-7b --seq 1024 --n=500
```
lee: thanks all. I'll follow up with AcmeCorp and attach the incident link when ready.
toni: logging infra notes — driver rollout change tracked in infra-rollouts ticket #IR-450. will freeze rollout until bisect finishes.
(closure)
max: good catch team — make sure the kernel selector change has a p99 guard in future deploys.
